Lint a project's documents and scripts without running them

Source: R/lint.R
lints.Rd

Reads .qmd and .Rmd documents as text and returns the typed numbers, construct errors and other problems the rules of lint_rules() find. Nothing in a document is run.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'weft_findings'
print(x, max = 200, ...)

lints(
  path = ".",
  files = NULL,
  rules = NULL,
  tier = 1,
  reader = c("weft", "pandoc")
)

Arguments

x

A weft_findings.

max

The most findings printed.

...

Not used.

path

One existing file or folder. The project root is found from it.

files

NULL, or documents and scripts (relative to the root or absolute under it) to report on. File-scope rules run on these only; project-scope rules still read every document.

rules

NULL (every rule of the tiers asked for), or ids from lint_rules().

tier

A subset of 1:2. The default is tier 1.

reader

"weft" (the default) or "pandoc".

Value

A weft_findings data frame sorted by file, line, column and rule, with columns file, line, col, end_line, rule, tier, spec, context, text, message, hint and sentence, and the attribute notes.

Details

The .R and .r files of the project (its scripts) are read too, for the literal strings they pass to weft() and for their claim() calls: in a script, weft("We found 12 sites") is prose like any other and its 12 is a finding, placed at its line and column in the script. A call is weft(...), weft::weft(...) or weft:::weft(...), or the right-hand side of a pipe; the argument read is the one R matches to x, a string literal (a raw string too) or the literal elements of a c(). Of the rest of a script's code only its claim() calls are read, by inert-check alone; phrases and strings given to other functions are not. The rules that read scripts are those with scripts TRUE in lint_rules(); the project rules read documents only. A script is left out when it is in a folder whose name starts with . or _, or in renv, packrat, node_modules, _site, _book, _freeze or _extensions, when its file name starts with ., or when it matches the setting scripts_skip of the _weft.yml nearest to it: a list of folder or file names, or paths from that folder, with no wildcards. Its default is [tests], [] reads every script, and a list that is given replaces the default, so keep tests in it. A skipped or excluded script named in files or as path gives a note. A script whose bytes hold neither weft nor a claim( call is not read; one that is not valid UTF-8 gives the read finding when its bytes hold weft and is otherwise not read; one that does not parse as R gives a note and no findings.
